artifacts.summary: Follow-up research: zot v0.10.0 is now installed and live (the seed report's one remaining hard blocker has resolved); discovered a bigger blocker for work item 3 -- the entire literature extension is absent from the deployed .claude/ tree and untracked in .claude-extensions.json, so the default headless deploy flow cannot activate it; confirmed zot's live-database-backed search/duplicates commands are a ready-made DOI-dedup building block; confirmed the freshness export is still stale; documented new zot v0.10.0 flags (--via-bridge, zot schema) not reflected in extension docs.

memory_candidates.content: In this repo, deploy-headless.sh's default (non-destructive) mode only force-resyncs extensions already marked active in .claude-extensions.json (plus bootstraps 'core' unconditionally). It CANNOT activate a brand-new extension that has no entry in that file -- resync_all skips anything not already tracked as active. First-time activation requires either the interactive <leader>al picker (which calls manager.load and durably registers the extension), or a deliberate headless call to manager.load(name, {confirm=false}) (the same mechanism deploy-headless.sh already uses internally to bootstrap 'core'). A documented 'Deployment Status: Active' claim in an extension's own README is NOT reliable evidence the extension is actually deployed in the live .claude/ tree -- it can drift arbitrarily once the extension is untracked in .claude-extensions.json. Always cross-check against .claude-extensions.json's active-extension keys and a direct filesystem check of .claude/ before trusting a README's deployment table.

The zotero-cli-cc (zot) CLI ships a 'zot schema <command>' introspection command (e.g. 'zot schema add') that emits machine-readable param schemas (types, flags, since-version, safety_tier) for any subcommand -- a durable way to re-verify a wrapper script's flag assumptions against the installed zot version without re-deriving them from --help text by hand. It documents input params only, not output/response envelope shapes -- confirming .data.* field names in a write-command's response still requires an actual (or --dry-run, which only shows a preview 'would' object, not the real envelope) live call.

zot's read commands (search, list, duplicates, stats) resolve their own data directory via 'zot config show' independently of any extension-specific ZOT_DATA_DIR env var or index file, and read the LIVE Zotero SQLite database directly -- never a Better BibTeX CSL-JSON export snapshot. 'zot search <doi>' and 'zot duplicates --by doi' are therefore immune to CSL-JSON export staleness and are ready-made building blocks for DOI-normalized dedup checks against a live library, without needing to hand-roll a Web API search or sqlite read. zot's search matching is case-insensitive but does NOT strip URL-scheme DOI prefixes (https://doi.org/...) -- callers must still normalize (lowercase + strip prefix) before querying, and should verify the .doi field of returned hits for exact equality rather than trusting substring-match presence alone.
